title: Cobre Panama production halt removed a major mine from active copper supply
summary: Panama’s Supreme Court declared the mine contract law unconstitutional on 27 November 2023, and Cobre Panama entered preservation and safe-management after production halted in November. Company and government records show that the interruption extended beyond the initial court decision.
materialityRationale: First Quantum reported 310 thousand tonnes of copper production through October 2023 and 331 thousand tonnes for the full year, then suspended Cobre Panama production guidance. The gate treats the halt as material because a producing mine and its dedicated export port left normal operation, without converting those figures into an unsupported price forecast.

claims.text: Panama’s Supreme Court declared Law 406, which approved the mining concession contract with Minera Panamá, unconstitutional on 27 November 2023 and announced the decision on 28 November.
First Quantum reported that Cobre Panama ramped down in November 2023, entered preservation and safe management, and had its production guidance suspended.
First Quantum reported approximately 121 thousand dry metric tonnes of copper concentrate remained unsold after disruptions at Punta Rincón port.
Panama’s Ministry of Economy and Finance reported no copper extraction or export during 2024 while the mine remained in preservation and safe management.
The observable transmission channel is a reduction in mine output and export availability; the cited record alone does not isolate a copper-price effect.

evidence.label: Supreme Court declares Law 406 unconstitutional
evidence.locator: Announcement dated 28 November 2023; decision issued on 27 November 2023.

evidence.label: 2023 preliminary production and 2024–2026 guidance
evidence.locator: Cobre Panama section: November ramp-down, P&SM status, 2023 production, suspended guidance, and unsold concentrate.

evidence.label: Panama Economic and Social Report 2024
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Economy and Finance of Panama
evidence.locator: Mining and quarrying section, page 27: operations ceased from late November 2023 and no copper extraction or exports were recorded in 2024.

impactPath.label: Production halt
impactPath.mechanism: Court action and operating constraints moved the asset out of normal production.

impactPath.label: Cobre Panama mine
impactPath.mechanism: The producing mine entered preservation and safe management after ramp-down.

impactPath.label: Punta Rincón port
impactPath.mechanism: Port disruption constrained shipment of already-produced copper concentrate.

impactPath.label: Copper supply
impactPath.mechanism: Mine output and export availability declined; price attribution remains unproven here.

impactPath.label: First Quantum Minerals
impactPath.mechanism: The operator lost production and sales contribution from the affected operation.

impactPath.label: Copper-consuming industries
impactPath.mechanism: Any downstream cost effect depends on inventories, substitution, other supply, and demand.

timeline.label: Supreme Court decision declares Law 406 unconstitutional.
The Judicial Branch publicly announces the unanimous decision.
First Quantum reports the November ramp-down, suspended guidance, and unsold concentrate.
Panama’s 2024 economic report records no copper extraction or export for the year.

contradictingEvidence: The sources do not establish that the halt permanently removes the mineral reserve or that reopening can never occur.
unknowns: The reviewed record does not establish a reliable restart date or long-term operating framework.
The reviewed record does not isolate the event’s effect on a specific copper benchmark from other supply, inventory, and demand drivers.
